title: The MUSA vLLM-Omni image pins the existing MUSA stack, so CUDA-only Omni kernels are excluded before any tuning starts
summary: The vLLM-Omni MUSA image builds vllm-omni with VLLM_OMNI_TARGET_DEVICE=musa against the MUSA base image and constrains the install to the already-present torch/torch_musa/torchada/triton/mate/vllm/vllm-musa set, then fails the build if any of them changes. Omni optimizations that depend on CUDA-only distributions such as flash_attn_3 or flash_mla therefore cannot be the mechanism behind a MUSA gain; the reachable levers are the generic or MATE-backed paths and the engine-side scheduling, caching and batching decisions.

hardware: Moore Threads MUSA GPU; the image does not state a single SKU
software: The MUSA base image that installs torch, torch_musa, torchada, triton, mate, vllm and vllm-musa
vllm-omni built from source inside that image with VLLM_OMNI_TARGET_DEVICE=musa
models: vLLM-Omni image, video and audio models served by this image
conditions: Applies to the Docker lane; a hand-built environment can still add CUDA-only wheels and is then out of scope
Does not claim that any particular Omni model serves correctly on MUSA

claims.description: The Dockerfile sets VLLM_OMNI_TARGET_DEVICE=musa for the vllm-omni build so setup.py does not fall back to CPU when no GPU is visible during the build.

It writes the installed versions of flash_attn_3, flash_mla, mate, torch, torch_musa, torchada, triton, vllm and vllm-musa to a constraints file, installs vllm-omni under that constraint, and fails the build if any constrained distribution changed.

Its smoke step imports torchada, torch, torch_musa, vllm, vllm_musa and vllm_omni and asserts torch.version.musa is not None, so a broken compat layer fails the image build rather than the serving run.

recommendations: State the image tag, the pinned constraint set and the vllm-omni revision with every Omni measurement; the constraint check makes any drift an explicit build failure.
Exclude optimization ideas whose mechanism is a CUDA-only distribution; they cannot be the cause of a change inside this lane.

Prefer engine-level levers that survive the constraint set: request and conditioning reuse, per-step work shared across denoise steps, tile or batch geometry, and the attention path the build actually ships.
Treat a CUDA Omni result as a hypothesis to re-measure here, not as an expected effect size.
validation_plan: Record the built image digest and the printed constraint list before measuring.
Profile one denoise step and one VAE decode step on MUSA to see which kernels are actually resident.
Run an AB/BA pair on identical prompts and seeds, checking outputs pixel-identical where the change claims to be lossless.
Repeat the pair after restarting the service to separate warm-up effects from the candidate.
limitations: Source-derived from the Dockerfile; this record was not validated by building the image or serving a model.
The Dockerfile at this commit may have been revised later; re-read it at the revision you actually use.
Constraint pinning proves dependency identity, not numerical or performance equivalence.
